steps.title: Partition TMRWDT into APB front-end, two timer instances, watchdog core, lock unit and IRQ/reset output logic
steps.goal: Write the Overview and Block Diagram. Fix the top-level partition: an APB3 slave and register decoder, two instances of one timer block (TIMER0, TIMER1), a WDT core (prescaler, counter, WARN/expiry logic, kick/window check), a WDT lock register, and the output logic for timer_irq, wdt_irq and wdt_rst_req. Confirm that everything runs on one clock, PCLK. List the design constants: KICK key, UNLOCK key, number of timers, and counter and prescaler widths.

spec_evidence.quote: two identical 32-bit general-purpose down-counting timers (TIMER0, TIMER1)
one 32-bit watchdog (WDT)
PCLK (up to 100 MHz)
protected by a lock key.

decisions.topic: Clock domain of the watchdog counter
options: Single PCLK domain for timers and WDT
Separate always-on WDT clock with CDC
decisions.choice: Single PCLK domain; the WDT counts on PCLK ticks generated by its PRESC prescaler
decisions.rationale: The spec lists only PCLK and PRESETn, and WDT PRESC is defined as 'Count every PRESC+1 PCLK cycles'.

done_when: The block diagram shows the APB decoder, 2x timer instances, WDT core, lock unit and output logic, with all inter-block signals named
Every top-level port (APB3 signals plus timer_irq, wdt_irq, wdt_rst_req) appears on the diagram
Parameters/localparams are listed: KICK key 0x5A5A_A5A5, UNLOCK key 0x1ACC_E551, 32-bit counters, 8-bit PRESC, timer count = 2
The Overview states that the design has a single clock domain

steps.title: APB3 port list, zero-wait-state timing and unmapped-offset PSLVERR decode
steps.goal: Define the APB3 slave interface: PSEL, PENABLE, PWRITE, PADDR[11:0], PWDATA, PRDATA, PREADY=1, PSLVERR. Define the address decode for the two mapped regions (0x000-0x028 and 0x100-0x118). Define exactly which accesses raise PSLVERR, and what side effects occur, for unmapped, RO, WO and locked accesses.

spec_evidence.quote: AMBA APB3, 32-bit data, 12-bit address offset, little-endian
Zero wait states (PREADY tied high).
PSLVERR is returned for accesses to unmapped offsets.
0x110 | WDT_KICK | WO

decisions.topic: PSLVERR scope for mapped-but-illegal accesses (write to RO register, read of WDT_KICK, write to a locked WDT register)
options: PSLVERR only for unmapped offsets; illegal accesses to mapped registers are silently ignored or read 0
Also return PSLVERR for writes to RO registers and to locked registers
decisions.choice: PSLVERR only for unmapped offsets. Writes to RO or locked registers are ignored without error. Reads of WDT_KICK return 0.
decisions.rationale: The spec mentions PSLVERR only for unmapped offsets. Silent ignore is common for lock-protected watchdog registers.
decisions.question: Should writes to read-only registers or to WDT registers while locked return PSLVERR, or be silently ignored with PSLVERR asserted only for unmapped offsets?

options: Decode PADDR[11:2] only, ignore PADDR[1:0]
Treat non-aligned offsets as unmapped (PSLVERR)
decisions.choice: Decode PADDR[11:2] only and ignore PADDR[1:0]
decisions.rationale: All registers are word-sized and APB3 has no byte strobes. Ignoring the low bits is the usual practice.
decisions.question: Should accesses with PADDR[1:0] != 0 alias to the containing word, or be treated as unmapped and return PSLVERR?

done_when: The port table lists each APB3 signal with width, direction and description, and states PREADY tied to 1
The decode table maps every offset in P7 to a register select signal; all other offsets are flagged unmapped
PSLVERR assertion is defined for the access phase (PSEL&PENABLE) and is shown to have no side effects on unmapped writes
Read data for unmapped, WO and reserved locations is specified as 0

steps.title: Register file field semantics: RW / RO / RW1C / WO / mixed WDT_STATUS and reset values
steps.goal: For every register in P7, specify storage (flop or derived value), the bits actually implemented, reset values (including WDT_LOAD and WDT_VALUE = 0xFFFF_FFFF and WDT_STATUS = 0x4), RW1C clear behaviour for IRQ_STATUS and WARN, and how reserved bits are dropped on write and zeroed on read. Specify the arbitration between a hardware set and a software clear of the same flag in the same cycle, and between a software write and a hardware update of the same register in the same cycle.

spec_evidence.quote: IRQ_STATUS | RW1C
0x114 | WDT_STATUS | mixed | 0x0000_0004
Writes to reserved bits are ignored; reserved bits read as zero.
7:2 | – | reserved, read 0
Window violation occurred (sticky until reset)

decisions.topic: Same-cycle priority between hardware flag set and software RW1C clear (IRQ_STATUS bits, WARN), and between a software write to Tn_CTRL.EN and the hardware one-shot EN clear
options: Hardware event wins
Software write wins
decisions.choice: A hardware set wins over an RW1C clear, so no event is lost. A software write to Tn_CTRL wins over the hardware one-shot EN clear.
decisions.rationale: This is the industry-standard choice for status flags. It avoids losing interrupts while still letting software re-arm a timer deterministically.
decisions.question: When a hardware event sets a status flag in the same cycle that software writes 1 to clear it, should the flag end up set (event wins) or cleared?

done_when: A field-level table covers every register: implemented bits, access type, reset value, and storage/derivation
IRQ_MASKED and WDT_STATUS.LOCKED are shown as derived (no own flop); WDT_VALUE and Tn_VALUE are read-only views of the counters
WIN_VIOL is specified as read-only and set-only, cleared only by PRESETn
The same-cycle priority rules from D4 are written as explicit next-state equations

steps.title: Timer block datapath: 8-bit prescaler, 32-bit down counter, zero/reload/one-shot and compare-match logic
steps.goal: Specify one timer instance in full. Cover the prescaler that generates a tick every PRESC+1 cycles while EN=1, and the prescaler restart on a LOAD write. Cover the counter behaviour: decrement, at-zero handling, periodic reload, and one-shot stop with the hardware clearing EN. Cover generation of the ZERO and CMP events, and the event outputs sent to IRQ_STATUS.

spec_evidence.quote: Writing Tn_LOAD loads Tn_VALUE immediately and restarts the prescaler.
When the counter is at 0 and a count tick occurs: the ZERO flag is set.
In one-shot mode the counter stays at 0 and hardware
When a count tick makes Tn_VALUE equal to Tn_CMP, the CMP flag is set.
15:8 | PRESC | Count every PRESC+1 PCLK cycles

done_when: Next-state equations for prescaler count, Tn_VALUE and Tn_CTRL.EN cover the tick, load-write and idle cases
The period is documented as (LOAD+1)*(PRESC+1) PCLK cycles in periodic mode
The MA states whether a periodic reload to a value equal to CMP sets CMP (tick-caused, so yes) and that a LOAD write equal to CMP does not, recorded in Assumptions
The prescaler behaviour when EN=0 and when PRESC changes mid-count is stated

steps.title: Timer interrupt aggregation: IRQ_STATUS / IRQ_EN / IRQ_MASKED and timer_irq level output
steps.goal: Map the four timer events to IRQ_STATUS[3:0]. Define IRQ_MASKED as IRQ_STATUS & IRQ_EN. Generate timer_irq as the OR-reduction of IRQ_MASKED, and wdt_irq from WARN gated by INT_EN. Settle whether the outputs are registered or combinational from flops.

spec_evidence.quote: | 0 | T0_ZERO |
timer_irq = |IRQ_MASKED[3:0]
level, active high, watchdog warning interrupt.
3 | INT_EN | Enable warning interrupt

options: Combinational AND/OR of status and enable flops (no extra latency)
Registered outputs (one cycle extra latency)
decisions.choice: timer_irq = |(IRQ_STATUS & IRQ_EN) and wdt_irq = WARN & INT_EN, both as combinational logic from flops
decisions.rationale: The terms are pure AND/OR of flop outputs, so they are glitch-free enough for level interrupts and keep latency at zero. This matches the spec's formula.
decisions.question: Must timer_irq and wdt_irq be driven directly from a flop, or is combinational AND/OR of status and enable registers acceptable?

done_when: The bit mapping of all four sources matches P10
The output equations for timer_irq and wdt_irq are written out, with the event-to-output latency in cycles
Clearing a status bit or its enable is shown to deassert the output in the next cycle

steps.title: WDT lock unit: key-based unlock, scope of protection, LOCKED mirror
steps.goal: Define the lock flop: reset to locked, cleared by writing 0x1ACC_E551 to WDT_LOCK, set by any other write. Define the write-enable gating for WDT_LOAD, WDT_CTRL and WDT_WINDOW, and which registers stay writable while locked (WDT_KICK, WDT_STATUS.WARN clear, WDT_LOCK). Define the WDT_LOCK and WDT_STATUS.LOCKED read values.

spec_evidence.quote: Writing 0x1ACC_E551 unlocks WDT_LOAD, WDT_CTRL and WDT_WINDOW.
Reads return 1 when locked. Locked out of reset.
Mirrors lock state

options: Only WDT_LOAD, WDT_CTRL, WDT_WINDOW (KICK, WARN clear always allowed)
Also block the WARN clear while locked
decisions.choice: Only WDT_LOAD, WDT_CTRL and WDT_WINDOW are write-protected. KICK, the WARN RW1C clear and WDT_LOCK are always writable.
decisions.rationale: P15 lists exactly these three registers.

done_when: The lock flop reset value is 1 and its next-state equation is given
Write enables for the three protected registers are gated by !locked
WDT_LOCK and WDT_STATUS[2] reads both return the lock flop

steps.title: WDT counter, prescaler and two-stage expiry (WARN then wdt_rst_req) control
steps.goal: Specify the WDT prescaler and the 32-bit down counter while EN=1. WDT_VALUE has exactly three update sources: kick_ok (valid, non-violating kick), wexpire (reload at expiry) and a tick decrement; a WDT_LOAD write and an EN 0->1 transition do not change it (per user answer Q1). Specify the first-expiry WARN set and reload, the second-expiry reset request gated by RES_EN, counter behaviour after a second expiry when RES_EN=0, and the sticky wdt_rst_req flop.

spec_evidence.quote: While EN = 1, WDT_VALUE counts down once per watchdog tick.
At the tick where WDT_VALUE is 0: if WARN = 0, set WARN and reload.
Once asserted it stays
1 | RES_EN | Allow reset request
0x104 | WDT_VALUE | RO | 0xFFFF_FFFF

decisions.topic: Effect of writing WDT_LOAD (or setting EN) on WDT_VALUE
options: WDT_VALUE changes only on valid kick, expiry reload or tick
A WDT_LOAD write loads WDT_VALUE immediately, as the timers do
Setting EN 0->1 reloads WDT_VALUE from WDT_LOAD
decisions.choice: A WDT_LOAD write does not reload WDT_VALUE; the new LOAD takes effect only at the next valid kick or expiry. Setting EN does not reload; the counter resumes from its current WDT_VALUE. Only kick_ok, wexpire or a tick change WDT_VALUE.

decisions.topic: Counter behaviour at the second expiry when RES_EN=0
options: Reload and keep counting with WARN still set (each later expiry re-checks RES_EN)
Stop at 0 until kicked
Wrap to 0xFFFF_FFFF
decisions.choice: Reload from WDT_LOAD and keep counting, with WARN left set. Any later expiry while WARN=1 asserts wdt_rst_req if RES_EN has since been set.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the watchdog live and periodic, consistent with the first-expiry rule and with the Q1 answer that wexpire is a reload source.
decisions.question: If the watchdog expires a second time while RES_EN=0, should the counter reload and keep counting, stop at 0, or do something else?

decisions.topic: WDT prescaler restart on valid kick
options: Restart the prescaler on a valid kick (kick_ok)
Free-running prescaler unaffected by kicks
decisions.choice: Restart the WDT prescaler on kick_ok, as the timers do on a LOAD write; a window-violating kick does not restart it
decisions.rationale: Gives a deterministic timeout after a kick and mirrors the timer rule in P9; consistent with violating kicks being otherwise ignored (Q2).
decisions.question: Should a valid watchdog kick restart the WDT prescaler so the timeout is exact, or should the prescaler free-run?

done_when: Next-state equations are given for WDT prescaler, WDT_VALUE, WARN and the wdt_rst_req flop, with priority among kick_ok, tick, expiry and RW1C
The WDT_VALUE equation contains only kick_ok, wexpire and tick terms; no WDT_LOAD-write or EN-edge term exists
The worst-case timeout from a kick to wdt_rst_req is derived as about 2*(LOAD+1)*(PRESC+1) cycles
wdt_rst_req is shown to have no clear path other than PRESETn
The reset values 0xFFFF_FFFF for WDT_LOAD and WDT_VALUE are reflected

steps.title: Kick key detection and window-violation logic
steps.goal: Define kick detection (a write of 0x5A5A_A5A5 to WDT_KICK), win_bad = WIN_EN & (WDT_VALUE > WDT_WINDOW) sampled in the kick write cycle, and kick_ok = kick & ~win_bad. A violating kick sets the sticky WIN_VIOL and asserts wdt_rst_req if RES_EN=1, and is otherwise ignored (no reload, no WARN clear) per user answer Q2. Define treatment of non-key writes.

spec_evidence.quote: Writing 0x5A5A_A5A5 reloads WDT_VALUE from WDT_LOAD and clears WARN.
If WIN_EN = 1 and WDT_VALUE > WDT_WINDOW at the time of the kick
A window violation asserts `wdt_rst_req` immediately if RES_EN = 1.

decisions.topic: Effect of a window-violating kick on reload and WARN
options: Flag the violation and still reload and clear WARN
Flag the violation and ignore the kick (no reload, WARN unchanged)
decisions.choice: A window-violating kick sets WIN_VIOL and asserts wdt_rst_req if RES_EN=1; otherwise it is ignored: kick_ok = kick & ~win_bad, so no reload and no WARN clear.

decisions.topic: Writes to WDT_KICK with a value other than the key
options: Ignored, no effect
Treated as a violation that sets the reset request
decisions.choice: Ignored with no effect and no PSLVERR
decisions.rationale: The spec defines only the key value and does not say that a wrong key is an error.
decisions.question: Should a write of any value other than 0x5A5A_A5A5 to WDT_KICK be ignored, or treated as a watchdog fault?

done_when: kick, win_bad and kick_ok equations are specified, including that the window check uses the pre-kick WDT_VALUE
It is explicit that a violating kick neither reloads WDT_VALUE nor clears WARN, and that with RES_EN=0 it only sets WIN_VIOL
Behaviour is stated for a kick while EN=0, a kick while WIN_EN=0, and a kick coinciding with a tick or expiry
WIN_VIOL is set-only, and both WIN_VIOL and the immediate rst_req path are drawn in the control diagram

steps.title: Reset and clocking: PRESETn-only reset of all state, including the sticky reset request
steps.goal: Document the single clock domain and the active-low reset style. List the reset value of every flop, matching P7, and the post-reset state: WDT disabled, locked, VALUE=0xFFFF_FFFF.

spec_evidence.quote: PRESETn, active low
Reads return 1 when locked. Locked out of reset.
Once asserted it stays

options: Asynchronous assert, flops reset on PRESETn low
Fully synchronous reset
decisions.choice: Asynchronous active-low reset on all flops, following APB convention
decisions.rationale: APB peripherals conventionally use async PRESETn. The upstream system is assumed to synchronise deassertion.
decisions.question: Should PRESETn be used as an asynchronous reset (standard APB) or a synchronous reset?

done_when: A table lists every state element with its reset value, consistent with P7
The text states that wdt_rst_req and WIN_VIOL clear only on PRESETn
The reset style and the deassertion assumption are documented

steps.title: Corner cases across timers and watchdog
steps.goal: Enumerate the corner cases and give the resolved behaviour for each. Timers: LOAD=0, CMP=0 coinciding with ZERO, LOAD write coinciding with a tick, one-shot re-arm, PRESC=0. Watchdog: kick on the expiry cycle, WARN clear on the expiry cycle, WDT_LOAD write mid-count (no effect until next kick/expiry), EN toggle mid-count (resume from current value), violating kick while WARN=1 with RES_EN=0, lock while an unlocked write is in flight. Bus: unmapped access, RO writes.

spec_evidence.quote: When the counter is at 0 and a count tick occurs: the ZERO flag is set.
At the tick where WDT_VALUE is 0: if WARN = 0, set WARN and reload.
PSLVERR is returned for accesses to unmapped offsets.

done_when: At least 12 corner cases are tabulated, each with expected behaviour traced to an equation or decision id
Every same-cycle collision (software write vs hardware update) for Tn_VALUE, Tn_CTRL.EN, IRQ_STATUS, WDT_VALUE and WARN has a stated winner
Cases derived from D7 and D10 (LOAD write mid-count, EN re-enable, violating kick ignored) are included

steps.title: Verification plan for APB register model, timer timing and watchdog safety behaviour
steps.goal: Define the testbench: an APB3 BFM, a register-model scoreboard, and cycle-accurate reference models for the timer and WDT. Define directed tests and coverage for every register access type, timer modes, watchdog two-stage expiry, window violation, lock key handling and the sticky reset request. Define assertions.

spec_evidence.quote: Once asserted it stays
If WIN_EN = 1 and WDT_VALUE > WDT_WINDOW at the time of the kick
Zero wait states (PREADY tied high).

done_when: The test list covers reset values, RW/RO/RW1C/WO/reserved bits, PSLVERR on unmapped offsets, timer one-shot and periodic modes with several PRESC values, CMP and ZERO flags, IRQ masking, WDT WARN to rst_req, window violation, lock and unlock, and invalid keys

steps.goal: Record each remaining defaulted decision (D2, D3, D4, D5, D8, D9, D11, D12) with its chosen behaviour and question, and record D7 and D10 as resolved by user answers. Record remaining spec gaps: Tn_CTRL[31:16] reserved semantics, WDT_CTRL[7:4] and [31:16] treated as reserved, CMP match on reload, and the absence of a debug-halt input.

15:8 | PRESC | Count every PRESC+1 PCLK cycles

assumptions.topic: PSLVERR scope for mapped-but-illegal accesses (write to RO register, read of WDT_KICK, write to a locked WDT register)
assumptions.assumed: PSLVERR only for unmapped offsets. Writes to RO or locked registers are ignored without error. Reads of WDT_KICK return 0.
assumptions.question: Should writes to read-only registers or to WDT registers while locked return PSLVERR, or be silently ignored with PSLVERR asserted only for unmapped offsets?

assumptions.assumed: Decode PADDR[11:2] only and ignore PADDR[1:0]
assumptions.question: Should accesses with PADDR[1:0] != 0 alias to the containing word, or be treated as unmapped and return PSLVERR?

assumptions.topic: Same-cycle priority between hardware flag set and software RW1C clear (IRQ_STATUS bits, WARN), and between a software write to Tn_CTRL.EN and the hardware one-shot EN clear
assumptions.assumed: A hardware set wins over an RW1C clear, so no event is lost. A software write to Tn_CTRL wins over the hardware one-shot EN clear.
assumptions.question: When a hardware event sets a status flag in the same cycle that software writes 1 to clear it, should the flag end up set (event wins) or cleared?

assumptions.assumed: timer_irq = |(IRQ_STATUS & IRQ_EN) and wdt_irq = WARN & INT_EN, both as combinational logic from flops
assumptions.question: Must timer_irq and wdt_irq be driven directly from a flop, or is combinational AND/OR of status and enable registers acceptable?

assumptions.topic: Counter behaviour at the second expiry when RES_EN=0
assumptions.assumed: Reload from WDT_LOAD and keep counting, with WARN left set. Any later expiry while WARN=1 asserts wdt_rst_req if RES_EN has since been set.
assumptions.question: If the watchdog expires a second time while RES_EN=0, should the counter reload and keep counting, stop at 0, or do something else?

assumptions.topic: WDT prescaler restart on valid kick
assumptions.assumed: Restart the WDT prescaler on kick_ok, as the timers do on a LOAD write; a window-violating kick does not restart it
assumptions.question: Should a valid watchdog kick restart the WDT prescaler so the timeout is exact, or should the prescaler free-run?

assumptions.topic: Writes to WDT_KICK with a value other than the key
assumptions.assumed: Ignored with no effect and no PSLVERR
assumptions.question: Should a write of any value other than 0x5A5A_A5A5 to WDT_KICK be ignored, or treated as a watchdog fault?

assumptions.assumed: Asynchronous active-low reset on all flops, following APB convention
assumptions.question: Should PRESETn be used as an asynchronous reset (standard APB) or a synchronous reset?
